title: SLA/SLO PRD for mixed-workload inference: dynamic tail budgets, probe-based canary checkpoints
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Define a measurable SLA and corresponding SLOs for a mixed inference workload (chat + embeddings + reranking) to enable safe progressive rollouts for model and runtime changes. This PRD captures latency envelopes, uptime targets, error budgets, instrumentation requirements, the canary probe plan, phased rollout checkpoints, and acceptance criteria for promoting changes to production.

Background: Mixed workloads exhibit divergent latency distributions (chat: low tail latency, embeddings: high throughput batched workloads). Past incidents showed config changes that improved throughput for embeddings caused regression in chat p99 tails for heavy-context requests. We need SLOs that are both workload-aware and tenant-weighted so rollout decisions reflect actual customer experience.

Objectives:
- Specify SLOs per workload class and a composite tenant-weighted SLO used for rollout gating.
- Define error budget computation with per-tenant allocation and accelerated burn detection.
- Design canary probes that exercise tail behaviors and validate KV cache/ batching/quantization impact.
- Define automated and manual rollback guards with clear thresholds and observability checks.

Scope (in):
- SLO definitions for three workload classes: interactive-chat, async-embeddings, reranking.
- Composite tenant-weighted SLO formula and rolling-window computation.
- Canary probe plan, probe queries, and automated checks.
- Required instrumentation and dashboard/alert definitions.
- Acceptance criteria and rollout gating policy for model/runtime changes.

Out of scope:
- Billing changes or pricing impacts.
- Deep model accuracy evaluation beyond simple checksum and latency-quality correlation probes (separate QA PRD).

SLO targets (initial proposal):
- Interactive-chat: p50 <= 50ms, p90 <= 180ms, p99 <= 420ms, availability >= 99.95% (1 month window).
- Async-embeddings: p50 <= 120ms, p90 <= 400ms, p99 <= 900ms, availability >= 99.9% (1 month).
- Reranking: p50 <= 60ms, p90 <= 200ms, p99 <= 500ms, availability >= 99.95% (1 month).
- Composite tenant-weighted SLO: weighted by monthly token-expenditure and peak concurrency; composite target: composite_p99_tail_index <= 1.0 (1.0 means no worse than baseline), availability >= 99.92%.

Notes on targets: Targets are intentionally tighter for chat tails; p99 thresholds based on observed baseline telemetry collected Jan-Feb 2026 with safety buffer for small-scale rollouts. Will iterate after initial canary runs.

Error budget policy:
- Window: 30-day rolling.
- Allocation: per-tenant budget = global_error_budget * (tenant_tokens / total_tokens) with lower cap for small tenants (min 0.1% of global budget).
- Burn detection: 15-minute accelerated-burn if burn_rate >= 2.0 for the 15m window OR if composite_p99 increases > 20% vs baseline for 5m.
- Protection: If tenant error budget exhausted, automatic traffic shunt to lower-tier model variant or subject to rate-limiting policy.

Measurements and signals:
- Required metrics: request_latency_ms (p50/p90/p99), request_success_ratio, token_count, kv_cache_miss_rate, batch_size_distribution, concurrency, queue_time_ms.
- Required tags: tenant_id, model_variant, region, workload_class, route.
- Windows: 1m, 5m, 1h, 30d rolling for different evaluation purposes.
- Baseline: rolling baseline computed using 7d median for each metric and workload_class.

Canary probe plan:
- Probe set: curated 120 queries split: 60 chat probes (long context, persona, multi-turn), 40 embeddings probes (varied batch sizes), 20 reranking probes (large candidate sets).
- Canary rollout stages: 0% -> 5% traffic (24h) -> 25% traffic (48h) -> 100% (48h hold). Each stage requires passing probes and no accelerated burn.
- Probe pass criteria per stage:
  - probe_p99 <= target_p99 * 1.10 AND probe_success_ratio >= 99.9%
  - KV cache miss rate delta <= 3 percentage points vs baseline
  - Batch size distribution not reduced more than 20% for embedding routes (to prevent throughput collapse)
- Automated checks run every 5 minutes during canary. A single accelerated-burn trigger or probe failure causes immediate rollback to previous stable variant and an alert to on-call.

Rollout gating and rollback criteria:
- Auto-fail conditions (immediate rollback):
  - composite_p99 increase > 25% sustained for 5m, OR
  - availability drop below 99% in any region for 15m, OR
  - error budget burn_rate >= 3.0 in 15m window.
- Soft-fail conditions (pause and require manual approval from PM + Eng lead):
  - composite_p99 increase between 15% and 25% for 30m, OR
  - per-workload p99 exceed target by 10%-25% for 30m.

Acceptance criteria for promotion out of staging to production:
- All probe pass criteria satisfied for 48h at 25% rollout.
- No auto-fail triggers and no more than one soft-fail event in any 24h window.
- Dashboards and alerts live with owner assignments and runbook linked.
- CI contract tests (latency regression tests using synthetic probes) pass in pre-prod environment.

Dashboards/Alerts and instrumentation tasks:
- Dashboard: Composite SLO overview, per-workload latency heatmaps, tenant-weighted burn chart, canary probe scoreboard. (Links: TBD, e.g., Confluence + Grafana URLs to be added).
- Alerts: Critical (pager): accelerated burn, auto-fail conditions. Warning (slack): soft-fail conditions and probe flakiness.
- Required instrumentation: ensure all inference routes emit unified metric names and tag sets; add probe endpoint and synthetic probe runner.

Rollout automation and guard implementation requirements:
- Automated traffic controller must support staged traffic shifts and immediate rollbacks via API.
- Canary probe runner should be able to pin probes to specific model variants and collect traces.
- Error budget calculation service must expose per-tenant budget and current burn_rate via API for automation to consult.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Overly strict p99 targets prevent shipping minor but safe improvements. Mitigation: phased threshold relaxation and manual override with formal sign-off for special cases.
- Risk: Probe corpus not representative of real tenant tails. Mitigation: include top-10 tenant real queries (anonymized) in probe set and continuously refine probes with production sampling.

Open questions:
- How should we treat large enterprise tenants that demand tighter SLAs (contractual overrides)? Proposal: add contract-specific SLO layer and exclude from composite tenant-weighted calculation for platform-wide rollouts unless explicitly opted in.
- Do we want an automated canary hold-for-slowest-region policy? Proposal: yes, add regional hold until all regions pass probe criteria.

Acceptance checklist (short):

- [ ] Probe runner implemented and dashboarded
- [ ] Automated canary controller integrated with rollout automation
- [ ] Error budget API available to automation
- [ ] Runbook and alerting owners assigned

acceptance_criteria: 1) Per-workload p99 and availability measurements reported for 1m/5m/30d windows and visible in dashboard; 2) Canary probe runner emits per-probe p99 and success ratio; 3) Automated canary stages enforce probe pass criteria before advancing; 4) Error budget API returns per-tenant budget and current burn_rate; 5) Rollout automation triggers immediate rollback on auto-fail rules; 6) Runbook created and on-call trained.
notes: Keep thresholds conservative for first two canaries; collect detailed traces on any soft-fail for root-cause analysis. Coordination required with sales for enterprise tenants that have stricter SLAs.
